findings.title: rules for ahead so each lives different otherwise reads for
findings.body: Returning early for `ACME_API_KEY`/`--api-key` skips `authenticate()` entirely, but the installer still enters the auth state and requires an access token (via `checkAuthentication` in `run-with-core`). In the common case where a user provides an API key without existing OAuth credentials, `acme install` now fails with an auth error instead of performing the login fallback that previously happened.

findings.title: it skips where and reads shape its so
findings.body: This unconditionally renames the active orphan environment to the fixed key `sandbox`, which overwrites any existing `sandbox` environment in the config. If a user already has a sandbox entry and later claims an orphan one, their previous sandbox API key/client settings are silently lost.

findings.title: matches envelopes that four record own each lives matches
findings.body: `opn` returns a promise, so calling `open(...)` without `await` means the `try/catch` won't handle async failures. When browser launch fails, this can surface as an unhandled rejection and the user won't reliably see the manual-open guidance.

review_output.overall_explanation: The new credential resolution path introduces a functional regression where installer auth is skipped when an API key is supplied, causing install failures without OAuth credentials. There is also a config data-loss edge case when claiming environments and a smaller reliability issue around browser launch error handling.
